LESSON: PHONOLOGICAL

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: LISTENING
Topic 1.2: Phonological

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Phonological. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. orally pronounce, blend syllables in spoken words and onset- rimes 3 lessons and groups 122
2. segment syllables in spoken words and onset rimes of single-syllable words
3. discriminate the initial, middle and final sounds in three letter words for correct pronunciation
4. add or substitute individual sounds in simple, one-syllable words to make new words. e) recognise and sound the commonly used letter sounds and syllables f) appreciate the sounds and syllables in rhymes, songs, poems, tongue twisters and riddles Core-Competence to be developed: Communication and collaboration: learners sound and segment syllables and words Learning to learn: learners blend and segment words Critical thinking and problem solving: learners form words from letter sounds and syllables

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. orally pronounce, blend syllables in spoken words and onset- rimes 3 lessons and groups 122
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to orally pronounce, blend syllables in spoken words and onset- rimes 3 lessons and groups 122. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. segment syllables in spoken words and onset rimes of single-syllable words
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to segment syllables in spoken words and onset rimes of single-syllable words. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. discriminate the initial, middle and final sounds in three letter words for correct pronunciation
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to discriminate the initial, middle and final sounds in three letter words for correct pronunciation. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

4. add or substitute individual sounds in simple, one-syllable words to make new words. e) recognise and sound the commonly used letter sounds and syllables f) appreciate the sounds and syllables in rhymes, songs, poems, tongue twisters and riddles Core-Competence to be developed: Communication and collaboration: learners sound and segment syllables and words Learning to learn: learners blend and segment words Critical thinking and problem solving: learners form words from letter sounds and syllables

Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Phonological.
2. Explain Phonological to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Phonological.
4. Show that you can: orally pronounce, blend syllables in spoken words and onset- rimes 3 lessons and groups 122
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Phonological. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Phonological important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. orally pronounce, blend syllables in spoken words and onset- rimes 3 lessons and groups 122
2. segment syllables in spoken words and onset rimes of single-syllable words
3. discriminate the initial, middle and final sounds in three letter words for correct pronunciation
4. add or substitute individual sounds in simple, one-syllable words to make new words. e) recognise and sound the commonly used letter sounds and syllables f) appreciate the sounds and syllables in rhymes, songs, poems, tongue twisters and riddles Core-Competence to be developed: Communication and collaboration: learners sound and segment syllables and words Learning to learn: learners blend and segment words Critical thinking and problem solving: learners form words from letter sounds and syllables

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
